title: His present wife, five children, and his son's mother in Little Rock
summary: Tate has been married since 1936 and has five children; he worries about the failing mother of his late son.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, my wife and I -- my present wife and I now, see, we got five children, see?
Oh, how long have you been married?
Since -- she's the one I married in '36.
Uh-huh. So we got about -- I think I got 11 grandchildren.

But for his mother, I don't think she's going to make it long. She's getting up in age. She was older than me. And I don't -- she doesn't have the will to live, she doesn't have the desire to live. She --

She's in Little Rock. And I actually want to call her because when I call her, it really makes her feel good. See, that was her only child and that's all she had. See, I got others, you know. And that -- but that was her only child and that's -- she adored him, her son, and she doesn't -- she kept saying, "Well, I'll be next." I said, "Don't say that. Don't think like that," you know, because -- then she went -- her sister put her in the hospital, time she got back to Little Rock. She stayed with him all during the time up to Silver Springs while he was ill, but as soon as she returned to Little Rock, she had to go in the hospital. So I just hope she makes it.
